north-driver.model: T1T11200350-15L: constant current 350 mA, 15 W, 120 V in, one channel, leading- or trailing-edge TRIAC dimming 100 % to 10 %, Class 2 output, FCC Part 15B consumer (spec sheet). The 1,100 lm level for homes and bars: the Vero SE 10 at 350 mA runs 26.0 V, 9.1 W [UNCONFIRMED: its output voltage window covers 26 V; power factor at 9 W (60 % load) for JA8's 0.90]

north-driver-575.model: ESS010W-0180-42 (round 42; the 575 lm level): constant current 180 mA, 7.6 W, 24-42 V DC out, 120-277 V AC in; forward-phase (TRIAC) and reverse-phase (ELV) dimming at 120 V AC and 0-10 V, 1-100 %; Class 2; FCC 47 CFR Part 15 Class B at 120 V AC (consumer); power factor over 0.9 and THD under 20 % (series figures); 'complies with ENERGY STAR, DLC and CA Title 24 technical requirements' (ERP's series page; JA8 itself is not named). At 180 mA the Vero SE 10 makes about 590 lm (about 3 % over 575) at about 24.6 V, about 4.4 W. CAUTION: 24.6 V is about 0.6 V over the driver's 24 V floor, and the COB's voltage falls as it warms and varies by bin: bench-test the regulation at Tc 25 and 85 C on three COBs from the production bin before committing (not yet tested)
north-driver-575.alternate: EPtronics LD6W120-36-C0170-TL: 170 mA, 22-36 V (a comfortable window for 24.5 V), 6 W, 120 V AC, TRIAC/ELV phase dimming, US Class 2, UL 8750 / UL 1310 recognized (Type HL), FCC Part 15 Class B at 120 V AC, PF 0.90 or more, THD under 20 %, 82 % efficient (EPtronics LD6W-TL datasheet). But it dims only to about 15 % ('<15% to ~100% CCR'), short of the 10 % JA8 and the brief ask; about 560 lm at 170 mA
north-driver-575.note: No 175 mA phase-dimmable Class 2 part was found (round 42, public datasheets): the ERP part meets every line on paper but its voltage headroom; the EPtronics part meets every line but its dimming depth. The Hatch XTC16-0350P-UNV-I (I-LOC key, 20-46 V, keys 50 to 100 % of 350 mA) may reach 175 mA but its key list, FCC class and dimming depth were not published on the page read | REVIEW 2026-11-01: with the Gen 7 Vero 10 at 24.2 V hot (typical) and about 23.0 V (low bin), the 24 V floor fails on low bins: bin-select the COBs (Vf 24.5 V or more at 180 mA, Tc 85 C), or choose a 180 mA driver whose window reaches about 21 V. Check its output ripple against JA8's flicker limit (under 30 % at every dimming level) on the bench.

core-cells.maker: any reputable LiFePO4 maker (to qualify: A123/Lithium Werks, EVE, Lishen)
core-cells.model: RETIRED in round 41 (the 48 base of rounds 35 to 39; the line now uses core-cells-18650). Three LiFePO4 26650 cells (IFR26650), about 3,000 mAh at 3.2 V each, in parallel (1S3P): about 29 Wh; about 2,000 cycles to 80 % (several times ordinary Li-ion's 500 or so); each to IEC 62133-2 and UN 38.3 (a UN 38.3 test summary from the cell maker). Each cell about 9.6 Wh (at most 20 Wh) and the set about 29 Wh (at most 100 Wh): Core ships under the small-battery exception (49 CFR 173.185(c), UN3481, contained in equipment), not as fully regulated Class 9

core-holder.model: RETIRED in round 41 (the 48 base of rounds 35 to 39; the line now uses core-holder-18650). A moulded holder for three 26650 cells with spring contacts, keyed for polarity, its NTC against the cells, wired to the board

south-weld.model: Hemisphere South (dropped 2026-10-25, a record): Welding South's shade: the skin, the crown weld ring and the opal liner, and the shell and the liner at the rim, with a polymerising acrylic cement (Acrifix 192 kind), cured, annealed and polished; a pull test of the first shades at 4 times their weight after 50 cycles of 25 to 60 C

core-cells-18650.model: PSL-FP-IFR18650EC (round 42), three in parallel (1S3P): LiFePO4 18650 energy cell, 3.2 V, 1.5 Ah rated, 4.8 Wh each, 14.4 Wh the set; 2,000 cycles at 100 % depth of discharge; 65 x 18.2 mm (flat top on its datasheet: Core needs a button-top cell for its shrouded + contact, so confirm a button-top version with Power Sonic or qualify another maker [check], review 2026-11-01), about 40 g; charge 3.65 V cut-off, at most 1.5 A (1C); discharge cut-off 2.5 V; charge 0 to 45 C, discharge -20 to 60 C. Approvals on the datasheet: UL 1642 cell certificate, IEC 62133 cell certificate (the edition is not stated: ask Power Sonic for the IEC 62133-2 report), UN 38.3 certified (the test summary, which 49 CFR 173.185(a)(3) requires a cell maker to make available, to request). Each cell 4.8 Wh (at most 20 Wh), the set 14.4 Wh (at most 100 Wh): the small-battery exception (49 CFR 173.185(c), UN3481, contained in equipment)
core-cells-18650.note: Capacity confirmed from the datasheet (1.5 Ah). Higher-capacity IFR18650s exist (a Bonrex IFR18650-1.8Ah sheet, 2020) but none found with published IEC 62133 / UN 38.3: Power Sonic's is the certified one

core-holder-18650.model: No holder (review, 2026-11-01): bare spring contacts in the milled base. The − end has a nickel-plated conical spring in a pocket; the + end has a gold-flashed leaf at the bottom of an 8 mm shroud 1.5 deep, so only a button top reaches it. The bays are 18.6 wide, 66.9 from the + leaf to the - wall (in the CAD); leads run in a milled channel to the board; the cells' NTC sits on one. Replaces the Keystone 1042, which is 77.1 long (its corners land outside the drum), not polarized (that is the 1042P) and surface-mount

core-board-18650.model: Core's board since round 41 (the 30 base), revised by the review of 2026-11-01: a USB PD sink at 9 V on the USB-C path and the dock's pins (an ideal diode on each input); the LTC4162-F LiFePO4 charger with power path (35 V max in), 1.5 A, 3.6 V; a coulomb counter (LTC2941 class [check]) for the gauge and the 90 % stop (4.05 of 4.5 Ah); per cell, back-to-back FETs under an ideal-diode controller (LTC4359 class [check]), off by default; the MCU on a diode-OR of the input and the cells; thermal foldback on a chassis NTC (55 C: LED to 70 %; 60 C: charge to 0.5 A) and the cells' NTC (no charge over 45 C); the warm-dim driver; capacitive touch with baseline tracking and a 50 ms debounce. Laid out as a 48 ring under the LED, the dock's pins on it (the axis and r 20), the USB-C on a flex to its small board in the corner at 170 deg

hemi-suspension.model: Round 43, PROPOSAL (certification.md): a 1.5 mm black-coated stainless suspension cable, 2 m, cut to the drop, with an adjustable gripper in the canopy and a fixed end in the cap; rated well over the fixture's 1.6 kg (Griplock's 1.5 mm kits are rated about 30 to 45 kg; to confirm on the part's sheet). The fixture hangs from it; the cord beside it carries the 26 V only

tint-chip-engrave.maker: a laser shop (a CO2 laser, 100 W or more)
tint-chip-engrave.model: Laser work on one Tint Library chip at about 100 sets: cut 80 x 50 R4 from 3/8" cast sheet (about 260 mm of cut), and the front's three lines engraved (the name, the code, LT at 9.5 and 3.2) and paint-filled

tint-chip-step.model: The step on one chip: a 35 x 50 flat-bottomed pocket milled from the back down to 3.2 (a 12 mm flat end mill, a vacuum fixture of 8), the floor fly-cut and polished clear, the edges polished

tint-card.model: The particulars card, 140 x 95, 600 gsm uncoated, letterpress or digital: the eight tints, each one's stock code, LT at both depths, and where EARF uses it

tint-felt.model: Four self-adhesive felt pads, 12 mm, under the tray

tint-mailer.model: A rigid mailer box with a foam insert for the case, 180 x 130 x 90

hemi-canopy-strap.model: Zinc-plated steel crossbar, 1.6 mm, screwed to the 4 in junction box; the cord grip, the suspension gripper and the canopy's screws anchor in it, and the driver and the 120 V splices sit in a closed steel enclosure on it. The black cast-acrylic canopy is a decorative cover only (black acrylic can't enclose 120 V splices) (review, 2026-11-01). No change to how the canopy looks

hemi-swag-supply.model: The plug-in swag (review, 2026-11-01): a 36 to 48 V Class 2 desktop supply (a 48 V 36 W level VI unit, GST36A48 class [check its Class 2 marking]) feeding a constant-current buck at 180 mA in the canopy (Mean Well LDD-L class [check the 180 mA setting]), which covers the COB's 23.0 to 26.9 V. Replaces 24 V and a buck, which can't drive a 24.2 to 26.9 V COB

hemi-tether.model: Review 2026-11-01: the shade's secondary retention, a 1 mm stainless wire-rope tether (7x7), crimped loops, from an eye screwed into the hub to an eye on the collar, slack in use; rated well over 10 x the 1.1 kg shade

hemi-driver-box.maker: to make (a sheet-metal shop) or a listed driver enclosure
hemi-driver-box.model: Review 2026-11-01: a closed steel enclosure, 92 x 64 x 37, 1.0 wall, zinc-plated, round the driver and the 120 V splices, screwed to the canopy strap; a listed bushing where the Class 2 cord leaves it

core-thermal-pad.model: Review 2026-11-01: two silicone gap pads Ø8 x 0.5, about 3 W/m K, electrically insulating (over 5 kV/mm), between the chassis's posts and the touch ring

core-tray.model: Review 2026-11-01 (UL 153 SA): a 0.5 mm 304 stainless tray formed round Core's three cell bays and the chassis's corners, open only at the aluminium hatch, so the cells sit in metal on every side; it holds them if the acrylic cracks in a drop. Fallback: a 0.4 mm UL 94 V-0 polypropylene liner (Formex GK class)

core-ball-two-layer.model: OPTION (2026-11-01, launch/stock-tints-lamps.md), for Ember, Poison, Haze and Smoke if the chips show the 'deep' case or 3/8 in isn't stocked: the ball in two layers, 6 mm clear outside on the existing mould and a 3 mm (1/8 in) stock-tint inner ball, frosted inside, on a second, smaller mould, 1 mm apart, joined only at the equator joint and the port's grommet (no bond across the face). Per ball, on top of the single-layer ball: the inner ball's forming and sheet about $15 to $25, the second mould about $1,200 spread over a run of 200 (about $6)

core-core-stock.model: OPTION (Core B, 2026-11-09): IN PLACE OF the formed core line, not on top of it. A stock Ø120 x 3 mm white opal acrylic sphere (the kind sold as a replacement lamp globe), if one is made in a full sphere or with a neck that cuts back to the Ø40 opening [check a supplier: none confirmed, no part number]; about $8 to $15 a ball [E], with no core mould. Against the formed core (about $25 to $40 a ball [E] and a core mould of about $1,300): it saves about $20 to $25 a ball and the mould. The opal must match Hemisphere's diffuser [check the grade]

core-dock-pins.model: Two gold-plated spring-loaded pins, about 1.5 mm travel, low force (about 0.8 N at 1.0 mm), on the pin board: + on the axis, - at r 20

core-pinboard.model: A Ø46 x 1.6 board under the chassis carrying the dock's two pins, wired to the main board's dock input (its ideal diode and PD path)

core-dock-contacts.model: 304 stainless, turned and lapped: a post Ø6 (+) and a ring r 18.5 to 21.5 (-), pressed into the dock, 1.7 proud of its pocket

core-dock-board.model: The dock's board: a USB PD sink asking 9 V (STUSB4500 or CH224K class), a resettable fuse, a load switch that powers the contacts only when it sees the lamp's 47 kOhm sense resistor, a USB-C receptacle at the back edge

hemi-ring-board.maker: Samsung (or Lumileds / Nichia equivalent, to choose)
hemi-ring-board.model: Hemisphere option 3 (the owner, 2026-11-10: "Core cut in half"): a flat Ø50 aluminium-core ring board, 24 mid-power 3030 LEDs (Samsung LM301H EVO class, CRI 90, 2700 K; 3000 K for Ice and Haze) on a Ø38 circle, facing UP into the shade at the mouth's centre, in two series strings of 12 at about 90 mA each (the ERP driver's 180 mA split two ways by the board's matched strings). Estimates to confirm on the datasheet [check]: about 42 lm a LED at 90 mA, so about 1,000 lm; Vf about 2.75 V, so about 33 V a string (about 31 V hot, low bin): inside the driver's 24-42 V window with about 7 V over its 24 V floor, about 5.9 W of its 7.6 W. Stock side-emitting (batwing) ring optic: none found with a downloadable IES file in one search (2026-11-10); the board is drawn and rendered bare until one is named | THE LED COLOUR PER TINT (the owner, 2026-11-10: "some need warm and some need amber"): amber 2200 K (CRI 90) for Ember; 2700 K for Poison and Fog; 3000 K for Haze; 4000 K for Dust, Acid, Ice and Smoke (the owner, 2026-11-11, on the Core colour test: a dye removes only what the source carries); the same lumens in every bin. The lens stays open: the board bare. Heat test needed: the hub about 6 K warmer than today (estimate)

north-driver-ring.model: ESS010W-0180-42 (the 1,000 lm level, 2026-11-10; the same driver): constant current 180 mA, 7.6 W, 24-42 V DC out, 120-277 V AC in; forward-phase (TRIAC) and reverse-phase (ELV) dimming at 120 V AC and 0-10 V, 1-100 %; Class 2; FCC 47 CFR Part 15 Class B at 120 V AC (consumer); power factor over 0.9 and THD under 20 % (series figures). It drives the ring board's two strings of 12 in parallel (about 90 mA each) at about 33 V, about 5.9 W: about 7 V over its 24 V floor hot, so the Gen 7 Vero 10's bin-selection caution no longer applies. Check the strings' current share on the bench (matched-Vf strings, or a small ballast resistor each)
north-driver-ring.alternate: EPtronics LD6W120-36-C0170-TL: 170 mA, 22-36 V (a comfortable window for 24.5 V), 6 W, 120 V AC, TRIAC/ELV phase dimming, US Class 2, UL 8750 / UL 1310 recognized (Type HL), FCC Part 15 Class B at 120 V AC, PF 0.90 or more, THD under 20 %, 82 % efficient (EPtronics LD6W-TL datasheet). But it dims only to about 15 % ('<15% to ~100% CCR'), short of the 10 % JA8 and the brief ask; about 560 lm at 170 mA
north-driver-ring.note: The COB (Gen 7 Vero 10; the Vero SE 10 was the wrong part in earlier text) is gone with option 3; the driver stays.
